title: Sharp zero-residue origin criterion for genus-zero Abelian differentials with higher-order poles
difficulty_reason: H2: the residue theorem alone does not impose the sharp maximum-zero-order bound for a differential with all residues zero. The author passes to a degenerate flat core, derives the necessity from the complete polar half-plane angle budget, and constructs the converse by cyclic polar-domain gluing. The three-zero case where merging any suitable pair would violate the bound requires a separate bipartite allocation of polar angles and zero valences; higher-zero cases then use the controlled merge/split induction. This constructive necessity-and-sufficiency argument is the new burden, rather than the elementary residue sum or the old one-zero simple-pole connection-tree theorem.
